title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
venue: Archival venue not independently verified here
access_depth: Primary author-repository README; paper full text not accessed
contribution: Biasing features can alter predictions while CoT omits their influence; repository includes BBH/BBQ prompts, samples and analysis.
limitations: Specific task/model/input-bias experiments do not establish all explanations are unfaithful. Paper full text was not accessed.
relevance: Motivates targeted tests for omitted decision influences and separates persuasive rationales from tested influence.
baseline_use: Controlled bias/hint influence stress test; not a universal metric.

title: Faithful Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
status: Author-repository acceptance report; independently verify proceedings
access_depth: Primary author-repository README; paper full text not accessed
contribution: Translator LM reasoning chains are executed by deterministic solvers to derive answers in structured tasks.
limitations: Faithfulness-by-execution constrains answer derivation but does not guarantee that translated premises correctly represent the input. Different from post-hoc classification explanation.
relevance: Connecting language, symbolic representations and executable checks is established prior art.
baseline_use: Conceptual comparator for verifiable-by-construction methods; not automatically a fair baseline for a fixed classifier.

title: On Measuring Faithfulness or Self-consistency of Natural Language Explanations
venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
status: Peer-reviewed publication metadata independently verified in official ACL Anthology XML
access_depth: Official archival metadata and abstract plus primary author-repository README; full paper not accessed
contribution: CC-SHAP compares Shapley input contributions toward the answer with contributions toward its explanation; code also implements earlier counterfactual, input-from-explanation, biasing and CoT corruption tests.
limitations: Attribution-pattern agreement establishes self-consistency, not guaranteed causal internal faithfulness. Masking assumptions and call/probability requirements matter.
relevance: Directly challenges using consistency or an explainer comparison as a faithfulness certificate.
baseline_use: Relevant self-consistency comparator where target-model access/compute permit.

title: Can LLMs Produce Faithful Explanations For Fact-checking? Towards Faithful Explainable Fact-Checking via Multi-Agent Debate
venue: Archival venue not independently verified here
access_depth: Primary author-repository README; paper full text not accessed
contribution: MADR generates explanations, uses debater critiques and a judge, then refines against evidence; defines source-related error types and uses PolitiHop.
limitations: Evidence faithfulness is distinct from causal faithfulness to a classifier. LLM critics may share errors and add cost; no audience-preservation claim verified in accessed text.
relevance: Very close prior art for generation→critique/checking→refinement; integration alone is not new.
baseline_use: Consider a budget-matched critique/refinement comparator; isolate adaptation-specific checks.

title: Tell Me a Story! Narrative-Driven XAI with Large Language Models
venue: Archival venue not independently verified here
status: Author README cites year2024; arXiv identifier dated2023; verify final metadata
access_depth: Primary author-repository README; paper full text not accessed
contribution: XAIstories implements SHAPstories narrative generation for target models exposing predict_proba, with example notebook and LLM API support.
limitations: README verifies implemented narration, not quantitative human-study results or checker efficacy. Conventional classifiers are not the thesis target LLM.
relevance: Strong prior art for SHAP-to-natural-language narratives and the separation of decision model from LLM explainer.
baseline_use: Translation-only design reference; do not silently substitute its classifier for the target LLM.

title: Faithfulness Serum: Mitigating the Faithfulness Gap in Textual Explanations of LLM Decisions via Attribution Guidance
status: Author-repository acceptance claim; independent record not yet inspected
access_depth: Primary author-repository README; paper full text not accessed
contribution: Counterfactual hint-influence tests plus PE-LRP attribution guidance injected into attention during explanation generation; open/closed model scripts.
limitations: Interventions need suitable open-weight access. README notes narrow useful strength range, with unstable or repetitive outputs if too strong. No universal guarantee verified.
relevance: Close recent prior art against novelty based only on attribution grounding or detecting hidden hints.
baseline_use: Strong access-matched comparator candidate; include among nearest work.

title: A Positive Case for Faithfulness: LLM Self-Explanations Help Predict Model Behavior
status: Author-repository BibTeX cites ICML2026; proceedings not yet inspected
access_depth: Primary author-repository README; paper full text not accessed
contribution: Evaluates whether self-explanations help predictor models simulate target-model behavior on counterfactual inputs; includes reference/predictor pipelines and simulatability analysis.
limitations: README/code description alone does not establish general fidelity. Simulatability depends on task, target, predictor and prompts.
relevance: Counterweight to assuming all self-explanations are useless; investigate when they predict behavior.
baseline_use: Complementary explanation-assisted simulatability evaluation if feasible; not direct access to hidden computation.

title: Are self-explanations from Large Language Models faithful?
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2024
status: Peer-reviewed metadata independently verified in official ACL Anthology XML
access_depth: Official archival metadata and abstract plus primary author-repository README; full paper not accessed
contribution: Applies self-consistency checks to counterfactual, feature-attribution and redaction explanations; reported reliability depends on explanation type, model and task.
limitations: Self-consistency is behavioral evidence and does not expose inaccessible internal ground truth; claims cannot be generalized across models/tasks.
relevance: Directly relevant baseline and prior art for target-model counterfactual/redaction tests; undermines treating simple reclassification as novel.
baseline_use: Reproduce an access-compatible self-consistency or redaction test, with precise operational terminology.
